usageRows.notes: Notion uses capabilities, not OAuth scopes; the user picks which pages to share during consent.
Same path as read & write; only the capabilities differ.

defaultUsageReason.text: Agents usually create and update pages, not just read them.

verdict.oneLiner: Self-serve: create a public connection and any Notion workspace can install it. No review unless you list it in the Notion Marketplace.

preApprovalLimits.text: Same limits before and after any listing: 180 requests/minute per connection (600 on Business/Enterprise).

steps.title: Copy the Composio callback URL
steps.detail: In Composio: Authentication management → Create Auth Config → Notion → OAuth2 → Use your own developer credentials. The redirect URI is https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback.

steps.title: Create a public connection in Notion
steps.detail: At app.notion.com/developers/connections → New connection: name it, choose OAuth (not API token), keep "Installable in: Any workspace" and add the Composio redirect URI. Then trim the default capabilities to what your agent needs.

blockers.text: Installation scope is fixed once created
blockers.workaround: Create a new connection if you picked selected workspaces

steps.title: Paste the client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the OAuth client ID and secret from the connection's settings into the Composio auth config and save.

steps.title: Connect a workspace and run one tool
steps.detail: Connect your own Notion workspace through the new auth config, check the consent screen shows your connection's name, and run one Notion tool.

steps.title: Ship it — no review needed
steps.detail: Any workspace can now install the connection through your Composio flow. Listing in the Notion Marketplace is optional and adds a security review.

gotchas.text: Installation scope can't be changed after creation; pick "Any workspace" if users outside your workspace will connect.
Switching from managed auth to your own OAuth app doesn't migrate existing connections: users reconnect, or you import their credentials where supported.
Each authorization of a new public connection mints fresh tokens; store the newest refresh token per user.
Refresh tokens can break if you change the connection's capabilities after users authorize.
The consent screen shows "backend.composio.dev" next to your connection's name. Use your own callback domain that forwards to Composio if that matters.
New connections default to reading user emails and inserting comments; untick capabilities you don't use.

unknowns: PKCE isn't documented; the token request uses HTTP Basic auth with client ID and secret.
Older Notion docs reportedly said public integrations need a security review; current docs limit it to Marketplace listing. We couldn't read the old version.

claims.text: Composio's Notion Toolkit supports OAUTH2, API_KEY auth.

sources.quote: auth_schemes: OAUTH2, API_KEY

claims.text: Composio offers managed auth for Notion.

sources.quote: managed auth: true

claims.text: Register https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback as the redirect URI (it stays on /api/v3/ even though the REST API is v3.1).

sources.quote: Register `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback` as the provider's authorized redirect URI.

claims.text: Switching to your own auth config doesn't move existing connected accounts; users reconnect, or you import their credentials where supported.

sources.quote: Existing connected accounts are tied to the auth config they were created with.

claims.text: Notion released a new API version on 2026-03-11 that replaced the `after` parameter in Append Block Children with a `position` object, removed the `archived` field in favor of `in_trash`, and renamed the `transcription` block type to `meeting_notes`.

sources.quote: The `after` parameter on Append Block Children is replaced by a `position` object. The `archived` field is removed in favor of `in_trash` across all request parameters and response bodies. The `transcription` block type is renamed to `meeting_notes`.

claims.text: The 2025-09-03 API update reorganized `/v1/databases` into `/v1/data_sources` for individual data source management and kept existing database IDs, introducing a new data source ID concept.

sources.quote: `/v1/databases` APIs are re-organized into `/v1/data_sources` (for managing individual data sources under a database container) and `/v1/databases` (for managing the database container.) Existing database IDs stay the same, but a new concept of data source IDs is introduced, and required in order to manage data source properties, to support multi-source databases.

claims.text: If a Notion OAuth app’s scopes or configuration change after a user authorizes it, existing refresh tokens can become invalid and require re‑authorization.

sources.quote: If the OAuth app’s scopes or configuration change in Notion after authorization, existing refresh tokens can become invalid and require a new authorization.

claims.text: OAuth integrations can start the authorization flow as soon as client credentials and redirect URI are configured; marketplace submission or review is not required.

sources.quote: Both scoped OAuth integrations and public integrations use this flow. You can start authorization as soon as you configure the integration’s client credentials and redirect URI; Marketplace submission or review is not required.

claims.text: Joining the Technology Partnership Program is optional and intended for companies interested in scaling a public integration with added support, not a requirement for API access.

sources.quote: This program is open to companies who have built a public integration and are interested in improving and scaling their integration

claims.text: A public connection can be created and used by any workspace without listing it; Notion's security review applies only to Marketplace listing.

sources.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace. You can create and use a public connection without listing it.

claims.text: Installation scope (any workspace vs selected workspaces) is set at creation and can't be changed; changing it means a new connection.

sources.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can't be changed afterward.

claims.text: Rate limit: 180 requests/minute per connection (600/min on Business and Enterprise), plus an unpublished per-workspace limit shared by all connections.

sources.quote: 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second)

claims.text: Since 2026-06-08, new public connections mint a fresh access and refresh token for each authorization.

sources.quote: New public connections now mint a fresh `access_token` and `refresh_token` for each successful OAuth authorization instead of returning the existing active token.

claims.text: Creating a public connection asks only for a name and development workspace, redirect URI(s), installation scope and capabilities; no business, publisher or domain verification step is described.

sources.quote: Fill in the required fields, including:

verifier.note: The fields are verbatim; 'no verification step' is inferred from their absence (hand-checked 2026-11-09)

claims.text: Creating a public OAuth connection was instant: the form asked only for a name, auth method (API token or OAuth), where it can be installed and redirect URIs. No company, privacy policy, terms or review step.

sources.quote: Create a connection to authenticate apps, agents, and workflows with Notion.

claims.text: The connection page states redirect rules: HTTPS only, and no URL fragments, relative paths, wildcards or public IP addresses.

sources.quote: Redirect URLs can’t include URL fragments, relative paths, wildcards, or public IP addresses.

claims.text: Redirect matching is exact: an unregistered domain and a sub-path of the registered callback were both rejected with "Missing or invalid redirect_uri".

sources.quote: Missing or invalid redirect_uri.

claims.text: A new OAuth connection defaults to read, update and insert content, read and insert comments, and user information including email addresses.

sources.quote: Read user information including email addresses

claims.text: The consent screen names the redirect domain ("Make sure you trust OAuth Runway test (backend.composio.dev)") and says Notion does not review third-party connections; the user then picks pages to share.

sources.quote: Notion does not review third party connections

claims.text: Notion's developer portal now lives at app.notion.com/developers/connections; "integrations" are called "connections".

sources.quote: Developer tools
